checks.name: product-authority
checks.summary: A3 PRODUCT AUTHORITY, derived and quoted with the file and line MEASURED (every line number in A3 agreed exactly with the Work Order; there is no disagreement in this item). docs/architecture/domain-model.md:265 ready = '優先順位評価済みで実行可能'; :266 active = '1つ以上のIncrementが進行中'; :267 waiting = 'dependency、capacity、time条件を自動待機'; :270 recovering = 'lost ExecutionやPreview failureから再開中'; :271 evaluating = 'Stableで課題が解決したか評価中'; :272 completed = '対応Stable ReleaseとEvidenceで課題解決を確認'; :275 '`failed`をRequirementの終端状態にしない。failureはExecution、Provider Run、Evidenceに記録し、Requirementはrecovering、waiting、needs-inputのいずれかになる。'; :101 '1 Requirementに複数Incrementを許す。Incrementが成功してもRequirementは自動完了しない。'; docs/product/user-facing-spec.md:272 waiting = '外部資源、依存、時間条件などを待ち、自動的に再評価される'; :275 recovering = 'failureまたはRunner消失後、安全な再開を行っている'; docs/product/definition.md:105 'Previewで実証され、Stableへ昇格した時点とする'; :111 '3. 利用可能なworkerが、実行可能なRequirementを排他的にclaimする。'; :130 '完了を自己申告だけで決めず、要求と不変条件を検証する'. THE FOUR CONCLUSIONS, stated plainly: (1) waiting is justified by a capacity or contention or dependency condition and by nothing else, so it is NOT a general 'nothing happened' bucket; (2) recovering is justified by a lost Execution or a lost Runner, which is exactly what internal/reconciler already writes when it expires a Lease past its TTL and calls domain.MarkExecutionLost; (3) completion is bound to a Stable promotion and is NEVER granted by an Increment succeeding; (4) an Increment existing at all is the precondition for the whole claim surface, which is why the severed Increment-creation path is the same defect as the two unreachable Requirement transitions. This reading does not differ from the design packet's, so no escalation is raised on A3.

checks.summary: A MEASURED DEFECT FOUND WHILE EXECUTING A20, REPAIRED IN THIS TASK'S OWN CODE AND RECORDED FOR THE LEDGER ELSEWHERE. The preview-local exercise failed on its first real run with 'GET /v1/runner/work never offered an Increment for requirement-... within 20s: the offer named 0 Increments'. The cause is an ADAPTER DIVERGENCE that every in-memory test in the repository is blind to. The port application.RequirementReadRepository.IncrementsForRequirements (internal/application/ports.go:123) is answered by internal/store/memory/store.go:466 with a filter on EITHER the Increment's own id OR its RequirementID, and by internal/store/firestore/store.go:707 with a batch GET of one document per id from the `increments` collection -- which answers ONLY Increment ids and returns NOTHING for a Requirement id. The two PRE-EXISTING non-test callers disagree accordingly: internal/application/readmodels.go:307 passes INCREMENT ids built from Requirement.Increments, and internal/reconciler/orphan.go:67 passes REQUIREMENT ids. REPAIRED HERE: internal/application/loop.go passes INCREMENT ids, derived from the page's own Requirement.Increments, which is the form BOTH adapters answer -- so no port change, no store edit and no new read, and a count measured against the in-memory adapter is the count the Firestore adapter reserves. The Increment batch has its own named bound, LoopIncrementReadBound = 200, because the number of Increments on a page of Requirements is not bounded by the number of Requirements; a page whose Increments would exceed it is TRIMMED AT A REQUIREMENT BOUNDARY and the cursor stops there, so every conclusion the pass draws about a Requirement is drawn from that Requirement's COMPLETE Increment set.
